finding: No official NFL price exists, so the price-snapshot store and the difference column are structurally empty.
impact: No edge can be measured; no strategy can be shown to beat a market; ROI against a market is impossible.
what_would_resolve_it: An official or explicitly licensed odds source, named in the ledger and added to the source registry.
owner_of_the_source: NFL (no public odds product) or a licensed operator

finding: The originated side went 28-44 (hit rate 0.3889) walking forward over weeks 5-9.
impact: The side model is worse than a coin flip at this sample. Any strategy built on it is harmful until the model changes.
what_would_resolve_it: A different rating method, validated on a held-out season, or a decision to stop originating the side.

finding: Every published number is in-sample. No forward sample exists, so gate G09 cannot open and no lifecycle decision can be made.
impact: Backtest results cannot support a promotion.
what_would_resolve_it: Time. Freeze the gate set and record 200 forward bets.

finding: Depth charts were captured for 2 of 32 clubs (NE, DET).
impact: The replacement-depth register is a two-club illustration, not a league-wide signal.
what_would_resolve_it: Capture the remaining 30 club depth-chart pages.

finding: The Week 10 injury report was only fully captured for WAS, NYG, NE and DET; the KC block was cut off mid-table.
impact: Injury coverage is partial, and every designation is a single snapshot that can change before kickoff.
what_would_resolve_it: Re-capture the full page and record a capture timestamp per club block.

finding: The deficiency_points penalty in the depth register is a declared weight that has never been validated against outcomes.
impact: It is a ranking aid, not a measurement. It appears next to real data and could be misread as one.
what_would_resolve_it: Regress depth deficiency on results once 30+ clubs are covered.

finding: The pricing model's sigma (13.5), home-field value (2.0) and shrink weight (0.75) are declared constants, not fitted parameters.
impact: The fair lines are reproducible but not calibrated.
what_would_resolve_it: Fit on a prior season and freeze before the forward test.

finding: Weeks 1, 3 and 5 on nfl.com render an explicit 'Hidden Score' placeholder in the score block, but the game headline carries the score inline.
impact: Scores were taken from the headline. If the headline and the score block ever disagree, the headline wins here and that choice is a human decision, not a fact.
what_would_resolve_it: Cross-check every score against a second official page (the game centre URL) before the next refresh.

finding: The NFL terms prohibit systematic retrieval of NFL content to build a database without written consent.
impact: This pack is non-commercial and informational, which the terms permit for the personal use clause, but the compiled CSVs are close to the line the terms draw.
what_would_resolve_it: Owner decision: keep as a private non-commercial archive, or seek written consent before any public/commercial use.

finding: COR-01 (win pct vs point diff) is near-tautological and is published only as a transcription check.
impact: It should never be quoted as a model finding.
what_would_resolve_it: Nothing; the label is the mitigation.

finding: The Week 10 slate has 14 games and 4 byes (CHI, DEN, PHI, TB). A 17-game, 32-team week would normally have 16 games.
impact: The count is what NFL.com displays; it is transcribed as-is rather than 'corrected'.
what_would_resolve_it: Re-read the by-week page; if it still shows 14, record the season structure as a known oddity.
